claims.statement: The shared chat-command registry supplies host parsing, `/help`, and platform advertisements where supported; `/reset-all-history` and `/pair` are hidden but remain executable, while `/model` is visible.

`/context-doctor` reads the active graph checkpoint to render bounded, content- and path-redacting context estimates without invoking the model or changing state; the host gives it 10 seconds, returns generic unavailable or failure messages, and does not interrupt an active turn.

The CLI attaches WhatsApp, Telegram, Discord, and Slack adapters from explicit flags or corresponding enabled environment variables; with no model it uses the echo runtime, while a model opens SQLite checkpoints and history, loads MCP tools, and builds the Deep Agents runtime.

Talon namespaces assistant state by a validated assistant ID under `~/.deepagents/<assistant-id>` unless configured otherwise, creates restrictive home directories, and keeps checkpoint, conversation-reset, and assistant-wide model-selection state inside that home.
Channel exposure is shared as `self`, `allowlist`, or explicitly acknowledged `open`; open exposure permits arbitrary senders to trigger the agent with operator credentials and local-host access.
Discord registers visible shared commands as native slash commands when enabled, whereas Slack exposes one `/talon` slash command and requires bot mention plus typed command text in channel threads.

A `/model` selection is assistant-wide, persists in host state, is restricted to a credentialed provider catalog plus the default model, and swaps a lazily built selected model and its context-aware summarizer into main-agent turns.

Talon loads MCP tools from the configured provider at runtime startup and exposes CLI configuration-path and OAuth-login commands; manual MCP configuration changes can be reloaded through `/mcp-reload`.

By default agent shell and file tools run on the host; configuring a sandbox starts a provider-backed session for the host lifetime and fails startup rather than falling back to host execution, while only assistant skills and memory are host-routed in the composite backend.

Talon is experimental and does not provide production-grade complete HITL policy, channel administrator controls, or multi-tenant boundaries; its sandbox does not cover MCP tools, and admitted channel access should be treated as access to the operator's credentials and host resources.

Sender pairing is limited to Discord, Slack, and Telegram DMs; operator approval consumes a channel-bound short-lived code, pairing grants allowlisted access rather than operator authority, and unreadable persisted pairing state fails closed.

MCP reload builds replacement runtime tools and graph under a lock; a refresh failure leaves the previous graph usable and marks the MCP reload inactive, while active tasks keep their original capabilities.

Inbound supported images are converted into bounded multimodal data-URL blocks, while outbound Markdown media must resolve to a supported regular file beneath the trusted outbound root and rejects URLs, traversal, and symlink escapes.

LangSmith tracing runs only when `LANGSMITH_TRACING` is truthy and `LANGSMITH_API_KEY` is present; each traced invocation is tagged and annotated with Talon assistant, conversation, trigger, and request metadata, while a missing optional package degrades to a warning without tracing.
The optional local activity logger records agent, model-lifecycle, and tool events; tool input/output previews are redacted, structurally bounded, and truncated to 1,000 characters.

`/smart-model` controls the assistant-wide model used by `ask_for_help`, independently of assistant-wide `/model`; the help tool is restricted to an operator main conversation and requires a channel approval before it sends the question to that model.

Slack uses Socket Mode, acknowledges envelopes before handling them, deduplicates recent event IDs, and treats a DM as one conversation while mapping each mentioned channel thread to its own conversation.

The host starts the agent runtime before adapters and the scheduler, unwinds already-started components after startup failure, and on shutdown cancels work before stopping channels, scheduler, and runtime.
A scheduler is attached only when at least one channel exists, and a scheduled result is delivered only through the channel serving its recorded origin; otherwise it is dropped.
Pairing state uses locked atomic updates, and the CLI warns that `pairing pause-jobs` must run while Talon is stopped because the live host is the cron store's only writer.

A new message in an active conversation cancels the existing turn, records an interruption marker after the latest committed checkpoint, and starts the new message on the same thread; a cancellation that exceeds 30 seconds blocks the new turn and requires a host restart for recovery.

ConversationSaver archives channel conversations so they survive restarts and context compaction; `/new` retains earlier sessions, while `/reset-all-history` deletes only the current chat's archive sessions and checkpoints and does not delete cron jobs, memory, media, traces, or backups.

Talon loads local and remote subagent definitions at startup; explicit reload validates and activates changes only for subsequent turns, retaining the previous valid configuration after an invalid edit and leaving running tasks on their original graph.

Tool approval policy is a per-assistant `tools.json` mapping of exact tool names to prompt requirements; updates use atomic compare-and-swap, become active on the next invocation, and invalid policy fails closed.
